items.text: Amirhossein Mousavi, a political prisoner held in Evin Prison, was sentenced by Branch 15 of Tehran Revolutionary Court to five years in prison and death for the charge of "corruption on earth." This sentence was communicated to him on 13 Aban. He was also sentenced to five years in prison for the charge of "insulting the sacred."

Mohammad Manan Raeisi, the representative of Qom in the parliament, wrote in a message addressed to Masoud Pezeshkian and Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf that several days have passed since the threat to the life of the community's Imam by the Israeli enemy, and so far there has been no reaction from them. He criticized their silence and called for a decisive response to the threats. Manan Raeisi also suggested that if there is no access to the White House, the palaces of their regional henchmen should be targeted.

Iranian media published a message attributed to Mojtaba Khamenei stating that hoping for a change in US behavior through party shifts or concessions is a "mistake." The message, released on 13 Aban, describes any concessions to the US as encouraging further demands and wars. Masoud Pezeshkian also emphasized that Mojtaba Khamenei has given new powers to the government for negotiations with the US.

The domestic production of super gasoline has started to be offered at gas stations in Iran; the CEO of the National Refining and Distribution Company announced its price as 103,000 tomans per liter and said that more than 70 stations have been equipped to offer it. The commercial manager of the National Distribution Company stated that the final price of super gasoline ranges between 103,000 to 110,000 tomans depending on transportation costs.

Ata Mohamad, an international relations expert, said that the shift of the congressional majority towards the Democrats does not necessarily lead to reduced pressure from Washington on Tehran. He added that Donald Trump might increase pressure on the Islamic Republic both diplomatically and militarily to achieve results.

Morteza Kazemian, a member of Iran International's editorial team, considers Mojtaba Khamenei's message as a collection of delusions, threats, slogans, and ideological positions and evaluates it as irresponsible from the perspective of national interests and the rights of the Iranian people. Kazemian assesses Mojtaba Khamenei's stance on the US elections as meaning an increased likelihood of renewed war and worsening economic crisis in Iran. He says the root of the crisis is the Islamic Republic and the ultimate solution lies with the Iranian people.

Shahram Khaledi said that the maximum pressure of the US against the Islamic Republic will continue for the next two years, and the Trump administration will neither withdraw military presence in the region nor stop economic pressure on Tehran. He added that Tehran's interpretation of the Democrats' victory as a sign of Trump's weakness could lead to intensified confrontations.

On Tuesday, 12 Aban, a group of greenhouse farmers from Golshan County held a protest in front of the Agriculture Jihad Organization building in Sistan and Baluchestan province in Zahedan. These citizens demanded solutions to problems related to fuel supply and allocation of their required quota.

An image sent to Iran International shows the tombstone of Amirhossein Ebrahimi, a protester executed by the Islamic Republic. Mizan News Agency reported the execution of Amirhossein Maleki and Amirhossein Ebrahimi in Isfahan. With these two executions, the number of those executed in connection with the "Alikhani Square" case reached 9.

Saeed Bashirtash, head of the Central Council of the Seven Aban Front, said the presence of Reza Pahlavi as a guest of the largest faction in the European Parliament was very important. He added that the main message of the speech was to convey the voice of the Iranian people and emphasize that the Islamic Republic is a serious threat not only to Iran but also to European countries and the international community. Bashirtash said European officials should end the policy of appeasement with the Islamic Republic and support the Iranian people.

Reports about reactions to the US election results on Wednesday 13 Aban have been published. It was said that Qalibaf referred to the American people's 'no' to war and that the Iranian people have suffered due to half a century of war-mongering by the Islamic Republic. It was also reported that Netanyahu was on the verge of ending the war with the Islamic Republic but Trump prevented it, and the Iranian people are paying the price for this political game.

Jean-Noël Barrot, France's foreign minister, said the Republican Party's defeat in the US midterm elections showed that democracy in the country is still alive. He added that this result should not divert Europe's attention from protecting its own interests, and if it does, it would be a serious mistake. Barrot emphasized the necessity of ensuring national independence and creating a stronger, more prosperous, and more democratic Europe.

The mother of Erfan Rezaei, a protester killed in the 1401 uprising, said in a video that her son loved life and consciously went to the streets. Azadeh Al-Ayoub had described the protesters as "drunk" individuals who threatened local residents.

Following the Republican defeat in the US midterm congressional elections, many questions have been raised about the possible impact of this defeat on Trump's campaign in Iran. Trump has said that the war with Iran played a role in the Republicans' defeat but he will veto the Democrats' plans. Hossein Aghaei, a member of Iran International's editorial team, has analyzed this issue in the Payvast program.

Mohammadreza Asprorin, head of the Alborz Province School Builders Charity Assembly, announced that the province still faces a shortage of 4,000 classrooms. Hassan Mehrani, CEO of this assembly, also reported a high density of students and a significant number of double-shift schools in the province. Mohammadreza Alborzi, governor of Chaharbagh County, said the county needs to build 22 new schools to meet the educational needs of students.

Hours after the Republicans' defeat in the US elections, Mojtaba Khamenei opposed any concessions and agreement with the US. At the same time, Trump, defending an attack on Iran, did not rule out the start of a third war with the Islamic Republic and said this decision would be in America's favor.

Real Madrid announced that Rafael Nadal, the Spanish tennis legend, has accepted the offer to join the club's board of directors. The final appointment depends on the approval of the club members' assembly on November 21. Nadal, 40, retired from professional tennis and is a longtime Real Madrid fan.

It was reported that yesterday, Kaveh Osmani, a citizen from Baneh county, was arrested by intelligence officers in this county and transferred to one of the detention centers of this security agency in Sanandaj.

Harana news agency reported the identification of Vahid Khodarikha, 34, one of three arrested protesters in Mashhad who have been sentenced to death on charges of "waging war against God." With his identification, the identities of two of the convicted individuals in this case have been confirmed, but the identity of the third person remains unknown. Vahid Khodarikha, along with Matin Farnian, 23, and another citizen, have been sentenced to death by the Fifth Branch of the Mashhad Revolutionary Court headed by Judge Hossein Yazdankhah in a joint case.

Reports indicate school closures and threats to deduct students' grades and spending resources to bring them to the November 4th ceremony. This occurs amid increased militarization and security atmosphere in schools.
The deputy commander of Fars police reported the arrest of a citizen in Shiraz for reasons including participation in the protests of Dey 1404, connections with opposition groups, and foreign media.

Andy Burnham, the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, said the results of the US midterm elections show that voters want to focus on the issue of living costs. Burnham added that he feels the world now has an opportunity to unite around the issue that affects all our lives, which is the cost of living.
A video received shows that during the compulsory November 4 march in Shahr-e Kord, a group of students responded to the government's slogans by chanting "Long live the Shah."

Following the death of Jesus de Miguel, the 30-year-old forward of Tenerife, major European football clubs paid tribute to him by publishing messages. A minute of silence was also held in stadiums and fans commemorated the player.

Kazem Alinejad, a political prisoner in Evin Prison, started a hunger and medication strike on 13 Aban in protest of being deprived of medical services and proper medical care. Prison officials have promised medical leave but have not fulfilled it. His diabetes has progressed, and doctors continue to prescribe previous medications without specialized examination.

Mohsen Rezaee, Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, said the great Iranian nation imposed a major strategic defeat on Trump in the battlefield and the Strait of Hormuz, as well as a heavy political defeat in Washington. He added that American citizens and the government personally bore the heavy costs of Trump's warmongering. Rezaee said anyone who confronts the Islamic Republic of Iran will pay a heavy price from the battlefield to their doorstep.

JD Vance, the US Vice President, identified the war with Iran as a main reason for the Republican defeat in the midterm congressional elections and said many voters who supported Donald Trump and him in 2024 voted for Democratic candidates this time. He stated that ending the war, focusing on living costs and inflation, prioritizing US interests, and changing the country's relationship with Israel were the four main demands of dissatisfied Republican voters. Vance also defended those in the Republican Party who called for a diplomatic resolution to the conflict with Iran and said criticism of support for a diplomatic solution was incorrect.

Mohsen Rezaee, Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, reacted to the results of the US midterm elections by writing that the Iranian nation imposed a strategic defeat on Trump in the battlefield and the Strait of Hormuz, and Americans had to pay the cost of his war. He added that anyone who confronts Iran will pay the price. Meanwhile, Iranian media published a message attributed to Mojtaba Khamenei stating that hoping for a change in US behavior through party shifts or concessions is a mistake.

Mohammad Qaedi, an international relations instructor, said the results of the US election go beyond a protest vote against Donald Trump and indicate the formation of a newer and younger identity within the Democratic Party. He stated that Republicans are now facing the challenge of redefining their political position. Qaedi emphasized that Trump must understand the message of the election and avoid repeating George Bush's mistake of ignoring voters' opposition to continuing the Iraq war.

Reports from schools in Hamedan, Tehran, Arak, and Eslamshahr indicate that students and teachers have been pressured to participate in the November 4, 2026, march and threatened with grade reductions or dismissal. Teachers report strict supervision by the education ministry and the influence of regime-affiliated forces in school management. Some students and teachers mention being taught political anthems and required to attend gatherings.

A video received by Iran International shows a group of schoolgirls singing the anthem "Nam-e Javid Vatan" together. In a significant number of schools across the country, singing this anthem has become one of the students' protest actions.

Agence France-Presse reported that the postponement of the 2027 AFC Asian Cup from January to December has made Hajime Moriyasu's future with the Japan national team uncertain. Moriyasu, who was supposed to step down after the tournament, may now hand over his position to Go Oiwa at the end of 2026. He stated that the progress of Japanese football is more important than his personal situation.

Democrats' victory in the US midterm elections and gaining majority in both houses of Congress has created a new challenge for Donald Trump. The Republicans lost even in their traditional strongholds. Iran war, inflation, and rising fuel prices were among the main concerns of voters.

A political earthquake occurred in the United States and the Democrats won the midterm elections with unprecedented results. Thus, the new US Congress with a Democratic majority can obstruct Trump's decisions, including the war with the Islamic Republic.
A video shows a group of students in Isfahan on Wednesday, 13 Aban, chanting "Long live the Shah" in the streets, coinciding with official ceremonies on that day.

At dawn on Wednesday, 13 Aban, the death sentences of four prisoners, including an Afghan national previously convicted of murder, were carried out. The executions of three of these prisoners were reported at Qezel Hesar prison in Karaj.

At least two protest gatherings were held in Tehran and Zahedan. On Wednesday, 13 Aban, literacy movement educators from various provinces gathered in front of the Ministry of Education in Tehran to protest job uncertainty. Yesterday, some greenhouse owners from Golshan county gathered in front of the Agriculture Jihad Organization of Sistan and Baluchestan in Zahedan to protest the non-allocation of greenhouse fuel quotas.

Some contract workers of Zahedan Municipality complain about two to three months of unpaid wages and demand payment of their wage claims. Also, some social security retirees in Alborz province criticized the lower amount of arrears paid in Ordibehesht compared to Farvardin.

A video received by Iran International shows that the fourth anniversary of the killing of the martyr Erfan Zamani was commemorated at his grave. He was killed on the evening of 12 Aban 1401 during the revolutionary uprising "Woman, Life, Freedom" in the city of Lahijan.

Prince Reza Pahlavi said in an exclusive interview with Iran International that the Islamic Republic's support for Russia in the Ukraine war and the expansion of Tehran's security threats to European soil have encouraged European countries more than before to change their policies towards the Islamic Republic. He emphasized that Europe's practical support should focus on maintaining Iranians' access to free internet, increasing economic pressures, and monitoring the assets of Islamic Republic officials. Prince Reza Pahlavi also said that for regime change, coordination of internal forces and the joining of military and law enforcement forces to the people are fundamentally important.

Donald Trump, the President of the United States, said on Wednesday, 13 Aban, at the White House that he knew from the beginning that the war with the Islamic Republic would affect the midterm election results but it was worth it, and if he could go back, he would not change his decision. He emphasized that the military power of the Islamic Republic has been completely broken and the goal of the military operation was to prevent them from obtaining nuclear weapons. Trump also said the Strait of Hormuz is open.

Two prisoners convicted of drug-related crimes were executed in Khorramabad prison. Also, two death row prisoners in Torbat Jam and Khuzestan were released after the victims' families pardoned them. A judicial official reported that 86 people have been spared from execution in East Azerbaijan since 1402.

Yesterday, the interrogation session of Azar Mansouri, a political activist, was held at Branch Two of Tehran's Security Prosecutor's Office. The case concerns the publication of a statement related to the December protests.

Dmitry Peskov, Kremlin spokesman, said that President Trump is still in power and expressed sincere hope that he continues his peace efforts. He added that the ground has been prepared for continuing negotiations and a new round of trilateral talks will be held soon.

The Iranian Short Film Association protested the issuance of a prison sentence and other punishments against Jafar Panahi. The association criticized judicial and security measures aimed at pressuring the artistic community and called for a legal review of the issued sentences. Jafar Panahi's lawyer announced last week the issuance of a five-year and one-month prison sentence and other penalties.

Chuck Schumer, a senior Democratic Senate official in the US, said on Wednesday, 13 Aban, that the war in Iran "must end" and noted that his party's future majority in Congress could use its control over the government budget to advance this goal. Schumer accused Donald Trump of unstable decision-making and said the American people do not know what they are fighting for in Iran.

Mohammad Hossein Sepehri, a political prisoner, was released today, Wednesday, 13 Aban 1405, after more than three years of imprisonment from Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad. According to the case documents, his release date was set for 18 Mehr 1405, but due to a case filed after he and Javad Lal Mohammadi were beaten inside the prison, his release was delayed by 25 days.

It was reported that the Republicans lost the US elections because Trump accepted mediation from countries like Qatar and Pakistan several times and stopped the war. Trump, by appeasing the Islamic Republic, gave it the opportunity to buy time and prevent Israeli attacks. Trump also thought he could reach an agreement by removing several layers of the Islamic Republic's leaders, but this structure is plagued by apocalyptic thinking from top to bottom.
A video sent to Iran International shows protesters in Tehran posting a notice on a bridge column that reads: "The regime's warmongering = destruction of the nation."

Benjamin Netanyahu, the Prime Minister of Israel, said in a video published on Wednesday, 13 Aban, that radical Islam threatens Israel from outside through the Islamic Republic and its proxy forces, and from inside through Islamist parties supporting "terrorism." He added that this movement is dismantling European countries and a similar threat exists against Israel. Netanyahu said Islamist parties cannot confront this threat.

Gol Gohar women's team scored their second goal against Persepolis yesterday with an exceptional team effort involving only 5 passes from their own goal area. The goal started with a pass from Fatemeh Adeli, followed by skillful passes from Shabnam Behesht and Zahra Alizadeh, who dribbled past the goalkeeper and assisted Afsaneh Chatrnor for the winning goal. This tactical move led to Sirjan's victory and Persepolis's first defeat, 2-1 in favor of Gol Gohar.
A video sent to Iran International shows that on Wednesday, 13 Aban, a sniper was stationed on top of a building for a government rally in Karaj.

Miad Maleki, former head of the US Treasury Department's sanctions targeting office, said that the sanction on the Turkish airport services company may disrupt Iranian flights to this country. According to him, the continuation of this company's services to Iranian planes depends on banking restrictions and the Turkish government's decision. Maleki also said about the sanction on the tanker flag forgery network that this network helped the shadow fleet bypass sanctions using forged documents, and the new sanctions could affect the Islamic Republic's oil exports for years and strengthen Washington's leverage in negotiations.

Alireza Nourizadeh said the Islamic Republic shows no sign of willingness to compromise despite the Republicans' defeat in the US Congress elections. He added that plans for attacks on sensitive targets in the Gulf countries and Israel have been proposed. Nourizadeh warned that targeting Arab leaders could lead to a widespread war in the region.

Abdul El-Sayed, after winning the Michigan Senate race, faces the challenge of fulfilling his promise to improve health insurance. He criticized Donald Trump and JD Vance in his victory speech. Advancing his promises may require cooperation with the federal government.

Morad Vaisi, a senior analyst at Iran International, said that the missile threats of the Islamic Republic against European countries have increased Western governments' understanding of Tehran's dangers and have caused the positions of Prince Reza Pahlavi in Europe to receive more attention. Vaisi added that practical support for the Iranian people must go beyond issuing statements and called for an end to the policy of appeasement, the closure of the Islamic Republic's embassies, and the expulsion of its diplomats from European countries. He emphasized that the determination of Iran's political future should be based on the people's vote.

A video shows a group of students on Wednesday, 13 Aban, simultaneously with a government ceremony, singing the anthem "Young Iran" at the eternal grave of Fatemeh Soltani. Fatemeh Soltani, 32 years old, was killed on 18 Dey 1404 in Esfarayen.

After the historic defeat of the Republicans last night, many of Trump's close associates, without directly criticizing him, considered the economic consequences of the Iran war as a reason for voter alienation. An interview was conducted with Shahram Khaledi, a researcher of Middle Eastern history and international relations, about the consequences of these changes.

BBC Sport reported that Tenerife fans paid tribute to Jesus de Miguel, the team's forward, at the Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez stadium after his death. De Miguel was severely injured during a match against Andorra on Monday after a collision with the team's goalkeeper and died on Tuesday from his injuries. Hundreds of people placed flowers, lit candles, and set up memorials for the player at the stadium.

Morad Vaisi, senior analyst at Iran International, said that after the failure to reach an agreement with Biden, the possibility of an agreement between the Islamic Republic and Trump has also decreased. He added that the missile threat against Europe has gone beyond analysts' statements and has been implicitly mentioned in a message attributed to Mojtaba Khamenei. This position will likely be repeated multiple times by Islamic Republic officials and commanders in the coming days.

Morad Vaisi, senior analyst at Iran International, said that Prince Reza Pahlavi considered regaining control of the streets the main issue in the path to overthrowing the Islamic Republic at the European Parliament. He also emphasized that in issuing the final call, two issues are important: a high chance of success and minimizing costs and potential harm to the people.
Murad Vaisi said in the audio version of Politics that Trump has a 60-day window for an attack.

On the second night of the fourth week of the UEFA Champions League, 44 goals were scored in 9 matches. Como defeated Lens 9-1. Manchester City won 3-2 against Leipzig and Arsenal beat Slavia Prague 2-1.

Two young men were reportedly executed on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, on charges of participating in the January protests in Isfahan. According to officials of the Islamic Republic, four security forces were killed during these protests. The lawyer for some of the defendants in this case has rejected the official narrative, stating that none of the defendants were officially accused of murder.

Shahir Shahidthales, an international relations analyst, said that the increase in energy prices and living costs due to the war with Iran were main factors in voter dissatisfaction and the Republican defeat in the US Congress elections. He added that the Democrats' victory could limit Donald Trump's ability to continue the war with the Islamic Republic, and Congress can use its budgetary powers to pressure government military decisions.

Democrats won with unprecedented results in the US midterm elections. The Democratic majority in the new Congress could limit Trump's ability to advance his plans. Kambiz Hosseini addresses questions about who holds the power to declare war in the US and reactions to the election results in a program.

Kamala Harris, Vice President under Joe Biden, expressed satisfaction with the geographic, ideological, and generational breadth of Democratic victories in the midterm elections and said these results cannot be categorized simply by party or country. She emphasized that Democrats must achieve tangible results in the economy and civil rights for voters from all demographic groups. Harris added that regardless of her decision about running in the 2028 presidential election, she intends to play a role in shaping the party's direction and highlighting issues where she has experience.

Donald Trump, the President of the United States, said on Wednesday, 13 Aban, that he can cooperate with the Democratic majority in the upcoming Congress on "many more issues than people think." He expressed confidence about the last two years of his presidency after the Democrats' wide victory in the midterm elections and regaining control of both chambers of Congress from the Republicans.

Isaac Herzog, President of Israel, on Wednesday, 13 Aban, responded to JD Vance's remarks about the need to change US-Israel relations by saying his country holds great respect for Donald Trump, President of the US, and his vice president. Herzog added that Israel has always tried to maintain the support of both US parties. These remarks came after Vance attributed the Republican defeat in the US midterm elections to the Iran war.

Haley Stevens, Democratic representative from Michigan, stated on November 4 that she does not regret supporting Mike Rogers, the Republican opponent of Democrat Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed. Stevens cited El-Sayed's connection to Hassan Piker and her support for Israel as reasons for opposing her party's candidate. She also said she will continue to fight against antisemitism.

Charlie Weimers, a Member of the European Parliament, in a video released from his meeting with Prince Reza Pahlavi, emphasized his support for him as an “alternative to the Islamic Republic regime,” stating: “We support your efforts to unite the people of Iran around a future in which they can choose their own government.” The Swedish MEP added that his belief in the parliament hearing the voice of an alternative to the Islamic Republic regime has grown stronger since he invited Prince Pahlavi in 2023. Weimers also said that Prince Pahlavi’s name has become inseparably linked with the hopes of many Iranians.

Donald Trump, the President of the United States, said on Wednesday, 13 Aban, in response to reporters' questions about the possibility of dismissing Pete Hegseth, the US Secretary of War, that he thinks Hegseth is doing a very good job. These remarks came after the Republicans' defeat in the US midterm elections, and speculation about Hegseth's future in Trump's administration has arisen. Trump also said regarding the possibility of appointing Hegseth to the vacant Senate seat of Tennessee that he would be very popular if appointed, but he has not heard anything about this possibility so far.

Ari Fleischer, former White House spokesperson, responded to JD Vance's remarks by saying the problem was not the Iran war but the ceasefire. He added the war should have ended six months ago with the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and the end of the Islamic Republic. Fleischer also called for removing second- and third-tier Iranian officials and US support for pro-Western forces.

Reuters reported in an analysis that China is trying to play a more prominent role in ending the Iran-US war, but Beijing's extensive economic influence over Tehran does not mean it can end the conflicts. Xi Jinping called for preventing the Persian Gulf from becoming a field of great power competition, and Wang Yi met with Iranian and Saudi officials. China has been Iran's largest trading partner for over a decade, but trade relations are not enough to force the Islamic Republic to reach an agreement.

South Korea's Yonhap news agency reported on Thursday, quoting the country's Ministry of Defense, that the anti-piracy unit "Chung-hae" will expand its operational scope and conduct operations in waters closer to the Strait of Hormuz. The South Korean government intends to present a plan to the parliament to extend the mission of this unit in the Middle East. The current mission of the Chung-hae unit is valid until the end of 2026, and the government will seek parliamentary approval to continue its deployment after this date.

Democrats in Texas set several historical records in the US midterm elections. James Talarico became the first Democrat from this state to enter the Senate after more than 30 years, and Gina Hinojosa was also elected as the first Latina female governor of Texas.

Abdul El-Sayed, a Democratic senator-elect from Michigan, welcomed Donald Trump's decision to halt military aid to Israel until the end of 2026 and called for stopping the sale of American weapons to the country. El-Sayed said arms sales should be stopped because they are used for genocide and apartheid and emphasized that the money should be spent on domestic needs. Trump had previously announced an agreement with Benjamin Netanyahu to stop annual aid of about four billion dollars but said arms sales would continue.

The US State Department sanctioned two individuals and one company on Wednesday, 13 Aban, for their role in efforts to supply man-portable air defense systems to the Islamic Republic. The department stated that Mohammad Ali Talboof, CEO of Armor Alliance based in Belarus, played a role in mediating between Chinese and Iranian companies to purchase hundreds of man-portable systems. The US State Department said the aim of this action was to prevent the rebuilding of the Islamic Republic's arsenal and to enforce the UN arms embargo.

JD Vance, the Vice President of the United States, said one day after the Democrats' victory in the midterm elections that the war with the Islamic Republic was one of the factors in the Republicans' defeat. An interview with Kambiz Tavana discussed the reactions of Donald Trump's administration officials to the election results.

Miad Maleki, former head of the US Treasury Department's sanctions targeting office, said that Beijing would reduce its oil purchases from the Islamic Republic if Washington increases pressure. He also emphasized that sanctioning intermediary networks for oil transfer raises the cost of evading sanctions and makes the transfer of oil shipments to buyers more difficult and costly.

HRANA reported the issuance of a death sentence for Vahid Khodarikha, one of the detainees of the December protests in Mashhad. At the same time, Amirhossein Mousavi's lawyer announced that his client was sentenced to death on charges of corruption on earth.

Sadegh Beigdeli, a lawyer and political activist, said that mere political positions are not a legal basis for labeling a group as terrorist. He also emphasized that increasing criticism of Israel in the US and some politicians distancing themselves from the country could challenge Washington's bipartisan support for Israel ahead of the 2028 elections.

Shahram Kholdi, a researcher of Middle Eastern history and international relations, said that the Islamic Republic has repeatedly misjudged the political divides in the US and faced strong reactions from Washington. He warned that any miscalculation by the Islamic Republic in the next two months could lead to heavy US attacks.

Donald Trump, the President of the United States, acknowledged the impact of the war with the Islamic Republic on the Republican defeat in the midterm congressional elections, and emphasized that he still defends his decision to start the war and does not intend to retreat from his position.

Navid Mohibi, a political analyst, said Donald Trump can continue military operations against the Islamic Republic for up to 90 days without congressional approval. He added that unlike JD Vance, Trump has no electoral considerations and if he decides to take military action again, there will be no obstacle in his way.

Reuters reported that China is sending a special envoy to Iran and Oman to expand its role in the Middle East. According to data from Kepler company, China purchased over 80 percent of Iran's maritime oil exports last year. Its annual trade volume with the Arab countries of the Persian Gulf has reached about 300 billion dollars.

Nico Paz, a Como player, displayed a jersey in memory of Jesús de Miguel, the late Tenerife player, after scoring against Lens in the UEFA Champions League. It was reported that de Miguel suffered cardiac arrest and died following a collision during a football match in Spain.

A group of citizens posted a video on social media showing that several trees in Shian Forest Park have been cut or burned. A member of this nature-loving group said that after following up with the responsible authority, the cause of this action was stated as "pest infestation."

The Judiciary Media Center reported the arrest of four citizens accused of promotional activities contrary to Sharia by making false and fabricated claims in religious and spiritual matters. Additionally, several other individuals related to this case have been summoned to the judicial authority.

Ali Parvin, former Persepolis coach, spoke about criticisms of Mehdi Tartaar during a farewell ceremony for Hassan Habibi at Amjadieh Stadium in Tehran. He said the team is at the top of the table and anyone can say anything. He added that the team can play poorly but if it gets three points, it matters, and asked if a team can play well and lose.

The US Treasury Department announced sanctions against several companies and individuals in India and Turkey for alleged cooperation with the Islamic Republic. These sanctions targeted a network in India accused of forging documents of ships carrying Iranian oil and a Turkish company for providing services to airlines sanctioned by the Islamic Republic.

Ali Shirazi, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said that American voters' dissatisfaction was not only due to the war with Iran but also due to Trump's contradictory policies in this war. He emphasized that Democrats and Republicans do not differ in their goals regarding the Islamic Republic, and their main disagreement is over the method of confronting Tehran.
A video received by Iran International shows that two students trampled on a paper flag of the Islamic Republic during the mandatory rally on 13 Aban.

Bahman Abdi, Director General of the Planning and Social Participation Office of Youth at the Ministry of Sports and Youth, stated that registering 13-year-old girls on matchmaking platforms with family consent is not necessarily a legal violation under current laws. In response to the removal of the "Adam and Eve" matchmaking app from Google and Meta platforms, he said that registration of girls over 13 with family consent can be legally reviewed and cannot be simply considered a violation. Matchmaking centers have been advised to raise the minimum age for accepting girls to over 15 years.

Pouya Norouzi was wounded by direct gunfire from Khamenei's suppression forces on 20 Dey in Nourabad Mamasani and died in the operating room. His name remains in the memory of this land and his memory is a guiding light for freedom seekers.

Amir Ghalenoei, head coach of the national football team, said at the farewell ceremony for Hassan Habibi that working in the national team is difficult and referred to Ancelotti who did not achieve results with the Brazil national team despite his resume. He also stated that the national team has undergone a generational change and youth promotion, and they intend to increase the pace of this process.

The media office of Prince Reza Pahlavi, in response to the death sentence of Amirhossein Mousavi, a political prisoner, called for breaking the silence and raising the voices of political prisoners at risk of execution. On Thursday, 14 Aban, the office wrote on the social network X that Mousavi was arrested due to his activities on X and his death sentence was issued based on "forced confessions resulting from torture" in the "show trials of the Islamic Republic." Mousavi's lawyer announced on 13 Aban that his client was sentenced to death on charges of "corruption on earth" through activities on the social network X.

The Islamic Republic Broadcasting aired a live symbolic execution scene of Donald Trump, the US president, from Tajrish Square in Tehran. This public display was held after the Republicans' electoral defeat in the US midterm elections. In the scene, a person wearing a Trump mask and prisoner clothes played his role while spectators closely watched the performance.

Hossein Aghaei, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said Trump, despite delivering heavy military blows to Iran's regime structure, failed to turn these achievements into a political and lasting outcome and by declaring a ceasefire, gave the Islamic Republic a chance to rebuild. He added that after the US midterm elections, Trump faces three options: agreement with the Islamic Republic, resumption of military operations, or continuation of the current situation with sustained sanctions pressure.

Morteza Kazemian, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said the Islamic Republic government is portraying the Republicans' defeat in the US midterm elections as if it had won the electoral campaign against Trump. He added that this triumphalist rhetoric does not reduce tensions with Washington and increases the risk of escalating tensions and military conflict. Kazemian also said that continuing the confrontation policy with the US will worsen the economic crisis and pressure on the lives of Iranian people.

Italian media reported the landing of an unidentified Italian jet at Mehrabad Airport and its eight-hour stop in Tehran. According to the newspaper Repubblica, the plane had turned off its transmitters at times during the flight from Rome to Tehran.

Mohammad Taghi Naqdali, a member of parliament, said there are "foot soldiers" in the streets of Europe and America willing to "bring American, Israeli, and European politicians to account," and the Islamic Republic is using these capacities. He stated that the response "without geographical limitation" can be carried out by missile or "visible and hidden hands" that are "close to the enemies." Naqdali said the economic interests and goals of America and Israel in the region are within the reach of the Islamic Republic, and Mojtaba Khamenei's order "has completely freed our hands to take practical action."
Aras Ahmadbeigi, an 18-year-old citizen from Ilam province, was released on Wednesday, 13 Aban, after posting bail.

As France prepared for nationwide strikes and protests on November 5, protesters in Paris set trash bins on fire and riot police were put on alert. French officials announced that about 70,000 police officers will be deployed across the country and between 500,000 to 700,000 people are expected to participate in protests outside Paris.

Gholamhossein Karbaschi, the editor-in-chief of Ham-Mihan newspaper, was sentenced by Branch One of the Criminal Court One of Tehran Province to one year in prison and two years of media activity ban. The prison sentence has been suspended for five years.

Benjamin Netanyahu, Prime Minister of Israel, said in his first video message after the elections that radical Islam threatens the security and Jewish identity of Israel from two external and internal fronts. He described the Islamic Republic and its proxy groups as an external threat and parties supporting terrorism as an internal threat.

Financial Times reported that Russia has sold 90 advanced guided missile launchers to Iran to expand military cooperation with the Islamic Republic. According to the newspaper, the timing and details of the delivery of these equipment are not yet clear.

Benjamin Netanyahu, Prime Minister of Israel, said in his first video message after the elections that extremist Islam threatens the security and Jewish identity of Israel from two external and internal fronts. Netanyahu also accused opposition leaders of preventing the formation of a national government by setting impossible conditions.

Yesterday, following indiscriminate shooting by military forces in the Kheirabad area of Iranshahr county, one citizen died and another was injured. Additionally, a relative of the deceased citizen was arrested after inquiring about his condition and transferred to an unknown location.

Cristiano Ronaldo retired from Portugal's national football team on Thursday morning before the announcement of the new squad by Jorge Jesus. After 23 years in the national team, he ended his international career with 234 games and 146 goals. Ronaldo won three championships with Portugal and said farewell to the Portuguese people in a five-minute video.

Badr Al-Busaidi, Oman's Foreign Minister, and Abbas Araghchi, Foreign Minister of the Islamic Republic, in a phone call requested "practical arrangements" for maritime safety and joint technical mechanisms to ensure the unobstructed flow of trade and energy. The official Omani news agency reported on Thursday, 14 Aban, that the two ministers considered moving beyond de-escalation towards sustainable understandings necessary. The purpose of these arrangements is to "end the state of war and prevent the recurrence of conflicts" in the region.

The victory of the Democrats in the US midterm elections has elicited varied reactions among Iranian citizens. Some criticize Donald Trump's indecisiveness and delay regarding the Islamic Republic, while others believe the change in congressional majority will not prevent the US president from military action. Mehdi Tajik, a member of Iran International's editorial team, examines citizens' reactions to the election results and their assessment of Trump's future policy towards the Islamic Republic.

Contrary to Iran's international commitments under the Convention on the Rights of the Child and the prohibition of using children in military affairs, 600 female students from Hamadan and Kohgiluyeh and Boyer-Ahmad provinces were sent to "Rahian-e Noor" camps in the operational areas of southern Iran. Additionally, 5,300 other students from these two provinces will be sent to similar camps in later stages.

Several managers of private hospitals have reported the accumulation of claims from insurance companies, continuous increases in drug and equipment prices, and the growing difficulty in covering treatment costs. A hospital manager said that none of about 35 insurance companies and contracted institutions have settled their 1403 debts. Managers also reported a 600% increase in the price of Ringer's serum over three years and daily changes in drug prices.
Saeed Hasani, a Bahá'í citizen residing in Shiraz, was released from Adel Abad prison in Shiraz after posting a bail of six billion tomans. This was reported by the HRANA news agency.

Ali Falih al-Zaydi, the Prime Minister of Iraq, ordered the Military Industries Organization to coordinate with the Ministries of Defense and Interior, the Popular Mobilization Forces, and other security agencies to determine armament needs and supply them from domestic production. The Prime Minister's media office announced on Thursday, 14 Aban, that al-Zaydi, during a visit to this organization, called for the development of domestic production and private sector participation. He also ordered that contracts be signed directly with manufacturing companies and that intermediaries be removed to reduce corruption.

Mohsen Ardestani, head of the Geographical Organization of the Armed Forces of the Islamic Republic, said Israel knows it will one day be destroyed by the Islamic Republic and tries to delay this event through negative propaganda and war.

A video released on social media shows the parents of the late Mani Safarpour washing their son's motorcycle, which had been covered in dust for months. Mani Safarpour, 18, was targeted during the protests on 18 Dey 1404 in the Salsabil neighborhood of Tehran.

Six members of the medical staff at Fayyazbakhsh Hospital in Tehran were sentenced to one year of suspended imprisonment and six months of service in charitable institutions following labor protests. Additionally, several hospital employees faced cooperation termination, administrative violation cases, and salary benefit deductions.

Hossein Rasouli Nasab and Mehdi Zarif, two detainees from the nationwide protests of Dey 1404 in Shandiz who have been sentenced to death, remain imprisoned in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad. Their death sentences have been confirmed by the Supreme Court and their cases have been sent to the execution unit. They were previously sentenced to death on charges including waging war through participation in destruction of public property and burning religious centers.

The Portuguese Football Federation reacted to Cristiano Ronaldo's retirement from the national team by issuing a statement calling for a ceremony befitting his professional career. The federation appreciated Ronaldo's 234 national games and 146 goals and stated it will not allow his farewell to be held without proper respect. The statement said this will always be Ronaldo's home and thanked him for everything.

Aram News, citing Iraqi security sources, reported changes in the leadership structure of Asa'ib Ahl al-Haq, Kata'ib Hezbollah, and Harakat al-Nujaba. These groups are trying to transfer some of their political, economic, and security responsibilities to new figures.

Mohammad Hossein Sepehri, a protesting teacher, was released from Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad on Wednesday, 13 Aban, after serving more than three years in prison. Sepehri was arrested by security forces in Mashhad in Mehr 1402 and transferred to Vakilabad Prison. He was sentenced by the court to a total of eight years in prison on various charges.
